reason: README offers a CPU llama.cpp GGUF deployment of the ~1B HunyuanOCR model with an OpenAI-compatible server, no gated weights.
demo: docs/llama_cpp.md (linked from README): build upstream llama.cpp, download tencent/HunyuanOCR, convert to GGUF, run llama-server base model (section 4.1)
goal: Following docs/llama_cpp.md (linked from the README), build upstream llama.cpp for CPU, download tencent/HunyuanOCR from Hugging Face (excluding v1.0/*; the optional DFlash draft may be skipped), convert it to hyocr-f16.gguf and mmproj-hyocr-f16.gguf with convert_hf_to_gguf.py, and serve the base model with llama-server as in section 4.1 (port 8080, alias HYVL, --jinja). /work/run.sh must start this server in the background and return only once it is ready to answer /v1/chat/completions on 127.0.0.1:8080 with an image input.
check: The hidden test sends one of the repo's bundled OCR test pages (llama_cpp/test_assets) with the official document-parsing prompt to the chat completions endpoint and verifies HTTP 200 and that the response contains the page's text.

revision.by: fairness review (every maintained-set exam re-checked against the source)
issues: Oracle depends on PIL (from PIL import Image...) inside the probe's env, but the documented conversion/client env installs only huggingface_hub, transformers, torch, openai (docs/llama_cpp.md section 2); a docs-following install without pillow fails the oracle with ImportError. The passing run installed pillow only because the check text said 'generated image'.

The repo ships 26 OCR test pages (llama_cpp/test_assets/ocr) and docs/llama_cpp.md 6.3 shows the expected output for ocr/0.png; v2 sends that page with the official doc_parse prompt using only the stdlib, which also exercises a real document page instead of two synthetic lines.
Goal adds 'modest ctx-size', which deviates from the documented section 4.1 command (--ctx-size 10240); removed. Check text updated to the bundled page.
